tasks.title: Meeting with Lisa - abt performance ratings
tasks.description:
Here is a structured, client-ready version of your meeting notes with a clear emphasis on Lisa’s rating context:

---

## **Key Discussion Points**

* **Improved Team Collaboration**

  * The team has transitioned from working in silos to a more **collaborative and interactive environment**.
  * Increased participation in discussions, with individuals gradually becoming more vocal and engaged.
  * A **safe and empowered environment** has been fostered where team members feel encouraged to speak up and share feedback.

* **Leadership & Team Culture**

  * Lisa has played a key role in creating a **positive, inclusive, and psychologically safe environment**.
  * Emphasis on **curiosity, ownership, and open communication**, ensuring no hierarchy barriers prevent participation.
  * Strong team culture built on **trust, compassion, and collaboration**.

* **Individual Contributions & Growth**

  * **Akhil**: Significant improvement; taking ownership of major technical initiatives (e.g., Angular upgrade, tech debt resolution), proactive in discussions, and strong in debugging/troubleshooting.
  * **Ashwini**: Transitioned from a quiet contributor to taking leadership in **contract redesign**, actively conducting demos and engaging stakeholders.
  * **Parminder**: Delivered exceptional work in **authentication refactoring and documentation**.
  * **Prashant**: Consistent and reliable support to the team.
  * **Sai**: Steady contributor; delivers consistently, though more introverted in communication.

* **Engineering Quality & Practices**

  * Ongoing efforts to **reduce bugs and improve code quality**.
  * Focus on **refactoring codebases** to enable better unit testing before QA handoff.
  * Need for increased awareness of:

    * Architectural issues
    * Code smells
    * Reusability and creation of global components
  * Encouragement to proactively raise **technical debt items**.

---

## **Performance & Ratings Context**

* Lisa highlighted that **previous performance ratings were given without having sufficient context or complete information about individual contributions**.
* As a result, she is currently **hesitant to provide definitive ratings at this stage**.
* Having completed **one year with the team**, and with prior management under Raghu, Lisa is focusing on:

  * Building deeper understanding of team members
  * Observing sustained performance and behavior over time
* A more **accurate and informed assessment is expected in the next evaluation cycle**.

---

## **Decisions Made**

* Continue fostering a **non-hierarchical, open communication culture**.
* Reinforce expectation that **all team members actively participate**, regardless of seniority.
* Maintain focus on **code quality improvements and technical debt reduction**.

---

## **Action Items**

* **All Team Members**

  * Actively participate in discussions, especially during refinement sessions.
  * Raise questions proactively when requirements are unclear (**no hesitation encouraged**).
  * Identify and log **technical debt and architectural concerns**.
  * Focus on writing **testable, maintainable code**.

* **Lisa**

  * Continue building **individual-level understanding** before formal evaluations.
  * Communicate expectations around **engineering quality and participation**.
  * Present structured feedback to the team on **areas of improvement and growth opportunities**.

---

## **Risks / Concerns**

* **Bug Volume**

  * High number of bugs identified; **root cause analysis not yet completed**.
  * Risk of recurring quality issues if not addressed systematically.

* **Passive Participation**

  * Some team members tend to **agree without full clarity**, leading to potential misunderstandings.
  * Risk of gaps in requirement understanding if questions are not raised early.

* **Limited Architectural Awareness**

  * Need for stronger capability in identifying **code design issues and long-term maintainability risks**.

---

## **Next Steps**

* Conduct **root cause analysis (RCA)** for bug trends and define mitigation strategies.
* Reinforce a culture where:

  * **No question is considered trivial**
  * Team members seek clarity during discussions rather than post-development
* Track and prioritize **refactoring and technical debt initiatives**.
* Reassess team performance with **more data-driven and informed evaluations in the next cycle**.

---

If you want, I can also convert this into a **client presentation slide format** or a **crisper executive summary (1-pager)**.

tasks.title: Links related to GenAI
tasks.description:
Found a tool that cut my AI code review tokens by 8x
🔥 𝗧𝗼𝗼𝗹 𝗗𝗿𝗼𝗽: 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗼𝗻𝗲 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗺𝗶𝘀𝘀𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗳𝗿𝗼𝗺 𝘆𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗔𝗜 𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗽
If you're using Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf on any real codebase - you need to know about this.
I tested an open-source tool called 𝗰𝗼𝗱𝗲-𝗿𝗲𝘃𝗶𝗲𝘄-𝗴𝗿𝗮𝗽𝗵 on FastAPI (1,122 files) and the results were wild.
𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺:
Every time your AI assistant reviews code or debugs something, it re-reads your entire repo. That's thousands of tokens wasted before it even touches your actual change.
𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗶𝘅:
This tool builds a local knowledge graph of your codebase using Tree-sitter. It maps every function, class, import, and call relationship into a SQLite graph. Then it exposes that graph to your AI assistant via MCP.
When you make a change, it traces the 𝗯𝗹𝗮𝘀𝘁 𝗿𝗮𝗱𝗶𝘂𝘀 — every file that could be affected — and your AI reads ONLY those files.
𝗠𝘆 𝗿𝗲𝘀𝘂𝗹𝘁𝘀 𝗼𝗻 𝗙𝗮𝘀𝘁𝗔𝗣𝗜:
→ 6,285 nodes and 27,117 edges parsed
→ 1,122 files narrowed to ~15 for a code review
→ 8.1x fewer tokens consumed
→ 100% recall on impacted files
→ Updates in under 2 seconds after initial build
𝗦𝗲𝘁𝘂𝗽 𝗶𝘀 𝟯 𝗰𝗼𝗺𝗺𝗮𝗻𝗱𝘀:
pip install code-review-graph
code-review-graph install
code-review-graph build
That's it. It auto-detects your AI tool and configures everything.
𝗪𝗵𝘆 𝘁𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗺𝗮𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿𝘀 𝗳𝗼𝗿 𝗮𝗴𝗲𝗻𝘁 𝗯𝘂𝗶𝗹𝗱𝗲𝗿𝘀:
If you're building AI agents that interact with codebases (code review agents, refactoring agents, debugging agents), this is a real-world example of how a knowledge graph + MCP integration gives your agent surgical precision instead of brute-force context dumping.
It has 22 MCP tools including blast-radius analysis, execution flow tracing, community detection, risk-scored reviews, and even auto-generated wiki from your code structure.
This is exactly the kind of architecture we talk about in the course — graph-based retrieval giving agents targeted context instead of reading everything.
𝗥𝗲𝗽𝗼: https://github.com/tirth8205/code-review-graph
Go install it, run it on one of your projects, and drop your results below. Would love to see what kind of graphs you get on different codebases.
Who's trying this today? 👇
